1.explanation: All of the overflow-scroll controls live inside the Tabs React class. The render() method emits two <button> elements when the tab list is overflowed, and it wires them up to the internal scrollListLeft and scrollListRight handlers. Because those buttons have no aria-label or other accessible text, screen readers can’t announce their purpose. To fix the issue you need to update render() (and/or the scrollListLeft/scrollListRight wiring) to supply each overflow button with a meaningful label (for example via an aria-label or aria-labelledby attribute).
1.bug_scenario: When the Tabs component collapses into its narrow/scrollable mode it renders “previous” and “next” overflow buttons (ChevronLeft16 and ChevronRight16 icons) as plain <button> elements without any visible text or aria attributes. Those buttons have no associated label (no aria-label, aria-labelledby or title), causing an accessibility violation.

2.explanation: The accessibility violation is caused by the overflow navigation buttons that are created in the Tabs component’s render() method: these <button> elements only contain an icon and do not include any aria-label, aria-labelledby, or visible text. To fix the problem, you must update the render logic in Tabs.js (and any helper methods that generate the prev/next buttons) to pass a meaningful aria-label (e.g. “Scroll tabs left” and “Scroll tabs right” via translateWithId) so that each button has an accessible name.
2.bug_scenario: When the Tabs component collapses into its ‘scrollable’ mode on narrow viewports, two overflow‐navigation buttons (with ChevronLeft16 and ChevronRight16 icons) are rendered as plain <button> elements with no visible text or aria-label. A screen reader audit reports “Form control element <button> has no associated label,” since these buttons have no accessible name.
